target: Ain al-Assad Air Base, Iraq; Erbil Air Base, Iraq
context: Retaliation for the killing of IRGC Quds Force commander Qasem Soleimani in a US airstrike (Jan 3, 2020). Iran provided advance warning through Iraqi government channels, allowing personnel to shelter. 16 ballistic missiles struck military facilities; no US fatalities. Over 100 US personnel later diagnosed with traumatic brain injuries.
significance: First direct Iranian ballistic missile attack on US military forces. Demonstrated Iran's willingness to escalate directly rather than solely through proxies.

target: Erbil, Kurdistan Region, Iraq (near US Consulate)
context: IRGC claimed strike on Israeli 'strategic centre' in Erbil. Target was near — but did not strike — the US Consulate compound. Characterized by analysts as political signaling during nuclear negotiations.
significance: Demonstrated use of precision ballistic missiles for political messaging. No Israeli facility confirmed at target location.

target: Red Sea commercial shipping; Israeli territory
type: Burkan-2H ballistic, Quds-1 cruise, Shahed-136 UAS, anti-ship ballistic
context: Following Hamas attack on Israel (Oct 7, 2023), Houthis began attacking vessels with perceived Israeli, US, or UK connections. US and allied navies intercepted many incoming missiles. Attacks forced significant rerouting of global shipping around Cape of Good Hope.
significance: Most extensive sub-state ballistic missile campaign in history. Demonstrated Iranian weapons transfer to non-state actors. Significant economic impact on global trade.

type: Ballistic missiles (~120), Cruise missiles (~30), Shahed-136/131 drones (~181)
context: Retaliation for Israeli airstrike on Iranian consulate in Damascus (April 1, 2024). Coordinated multi-layer attack over several hours. Intercepted by 4-nation coalition: Israel (Arrow-2/3, David's Sling, F-35/F-16 fighters), US (DDG Arleigh Burke-class SM-3/SM-2), UK (RAF Typhoons), Jordan (RJAF). ~99% of ballistic missiles intercepted; ~8 penetrated and struck Nevatim Air Base causing minor runway damage.
significance: First direct Iranian attack on Israeli territory. Demonstrated capability and limits of layered missile defense. Near-complete interception of ballistic missiles; several penetrated defenses. Operational analysis ongoing.

target: Israel — Nevatim Air Base; Palmachim Air Base; Intelligence HQ
type: Ballistic missiles — primarily Kheibar Shekan, Emad, Ghadr variants
context: Retaliation for killing of Hezbollah Secretary-General Hassan Nasrallah (Sept 27) and IRGC General Abbas Nilforoushan. All-ballistic salvo with no drones or cruise missiles — concentrated on saturating air defenses with fast-moving threats. Kheibar Shekan maneuvering warheads created targeting challenges for interceptors. Several missiles struck Nevatim Air Base.
significance: Lower intercept rate than True Promise I (~83% vs ~93%). More effective ballistic salvo with fewer overall missiles. Use of Kheibar Shekan demonstrated improved Iranian precision strike capability. Israel responded militarily October 26.

type: Kalibr cruise, Iskander-M ballistic, Kh-101/Kh-55 cruise, Kinzhal, S-300 surface-to-surface
intercepted: Partial — Ukrainian air defense (Patriot, NASAMS, Gepard, legacy Soviet)
context: Sustained campaign of missile strikes against Ukrainian critical infrastructure, military targets, and population centers following full-scale invasion. Kalibr cruise missiles fired from Caspian Sea, Black Sea, and submarines. Kinzhal hypersonic missiles used; one reportedly intercepted by Patriot PAC-3 (confirmed May 2023). Western air defense systems progressively transferred to Ukraine.
significance: Largest sustained missile campaign in Europe since WWII. Demonstrated vulnerability of civilian infrastructure to precision cruise missile attack. Tested and demonstrated limits of air defenses in contested environment.

context: Ukrainian Patriot PAC-3 system claimed intercept of 6 Kinzhal hypersonic ballistic missiles over Kyiv. Russia disputed the claim. US and Ukrainian officials confirmed the intercept. Significant because Kinzhal was marketed by Russia as 'unstoppable' — first known successful intercept of claimed hypersonic system in combat.
significance: Demonstrated that PAC-3 can intercept quasi-ballistic missiles marketed as hypersonic. Clarified that Kinzhal's 'hypersonic' designation is contested — it follows a ballistic trajectory, unlike true maneuvering HGVs.

type: Qassam rockets, Kornet ATGMs, long-range Badr rockets
context: Simultaneous ground, air, and sea infiltration with massive rocket barrage designed to saturate Iron Dome. The scale of simultaneous launches partially overwhelmed point-defense prioritization algorithms. Most casualties from the ground infiltration rather than rockets.
significance: Demonstrated saturation as a tactic against point-defense systems. Iron Dome's engagement prioritization correctly de-prioritized rockets headed for open areas, meaning some rockets to populated zones penetrated. Triggered conflict in Gaza.
